result.summary: The image depicts a signalized urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and continuous sidewalks. While essential infrastructure like pedestrian signals and curb ramps are present, the environment is characterized by a relatively wide crossing distance and a lack of physical buffers or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic at the intersection without a median refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the intersection corner.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, increasing their visibility in the crosswalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, continuous sidewalk fronting a row of residential buildings. While the walkway is unobstructed, the lack of a buffer from the roadway and the presence of a bus stop without enhanced crossing facilities present moderate risks.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire curb line in the foreground.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A parked car on the right side of the image may block the visibility of pedestrians, particularly children, from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom right corner of the image.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the bus stop area to improve pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Add street trees or planters along the curb to create a physical buffer and improve the walking environment.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with mature trees providing shade, but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. Parallel parking on both sides of the two-lane roadway creates potential visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the street can hide pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both the left and right sides of the street.

hazards.name: Lack of designated crossing points
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks or pedestrian signage over this stretch of road may lead to unsafe midblock crossings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to slow down traffic on this straight residential stretch.

result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban residential environment with a continuous paved sidewalk and parallel on-street parking. While the walkway is separated by a curb, there is no additional buffer between pedestrians and the roadway, and parked vehicles may create sightline obstructions.

hazards.description: The white SUV parked at the curb blocks the line of sight between drivers and any pedestrians who might attempt to cross the street mid-block.

hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the parking lane/roadway with no planting strip or furniture zone to provide physical or psychological separation from traffic.
